title: CDL license standards practice questions
description: Free CDL practice questions on 49 CFR Part 383: the single license, CLPs, vehicle groups, endorsements, disqualifications and tests, with sources.

questions.topic: Who the rules cover and the single license
questions.question: What limit does 383.21 set on the number of driver's licenses a person who operates a commercial motor vehicle may have?

options.A: No more than one driver's license at any time
options.B: One commercial and one non-commercial license
options.C: One license for each State the person drives in
options.D: Up to three licenses, if all are reported to the employer

questions.explanation: 383.21 says: "No person who operates a commercial motor vehicle shall at any time have more than one driver's license."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.21, Number of drivers' licenses (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person who operates a commercial motor vehicle shall at any time have more than one driver's license.

questions.question: What deadline does 383.31(a) set for a CDL holder who operates a CMV to notify the current employer of a conviction for a traffic control law violation (other than parking)?

options.B: At the next annual review of the driving record
options.C: Within 30 days after the date of the conviction
options.D: Within 60 days after the conviction

questions.explanation: The driver "shall notify his/her current employer of such conviction. The notification must be made within 30 days after the date that the person has been convicted." It applies to convictions "in any type of motor vehicle" and must be made in writing.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.31, Notification of convictions for driver violations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall notify his/her current employer of such conviction. The notification must be made within 30 days after the date that the person has been convicted. [...] The notification to the employer must be made in writing

questions.question: What deadline does 383.33 set for an employee whose driver's license is suspended to notify the current employer?

options.B: Before the end of the business day following the day the employee received notice
options.C: At the next license renewal
options.D: Only if the suspension lasts longer than 60 days

questions.explanation: The notification "must be made before the end of the business day following the day the employee received notice of the suspension, revocation, cancellation, lost privilege, or disqualification."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.33, Notification of driver's license suspensions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The notification must be made before the end of the business day following the day the employee received notice of the suspension, revocation, cancellation, lost privilege, or disqualification.

questions.question: What period of employment history does 383.35(c) require a CMV driver applicant to present to the prospective employer?

options.B: The 5 years preceding the application
options.C: The 7 years preceding the application
options.D: The 10 years preceding the date the application is submitted

questions.explanation: 383.35(c) covers "employment history information for the 10 years preceding the date the application is submitted", including the previous CMV employers, the dates of employment and the reason for leaving.

questions.question: For how long after initial issuance of the CLP does 383.25(e) make the CLP holder ineligible to take the CDL skills test?

options.B: The first 14 days
options.C: The first 7 days
options.D: The first 48 hours

questions.explanation: 383.25(e): "The CLP holder is not eligible to take the CDL skills test in the first 14 days after initial issuance of the CLP."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.25, Commercial learner's permit (CLP) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The CLP holder is not eligible to take the CDL skills test in the first 14 days after initial issuance of the CLP.

questions.question: What is the longest a CLP may be valid from its initial date of issuance without the holder having to retake the general and endorsement knowledge tests?

options.B: 18 months
options.C: Two years
options.D: Four years

questions.explanation: "The CLP must be valid for no more than one year from the initial date of issuance without requiring the CLP holder to retake the general and endorsement knowledge tests."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.25, Commercial learner's permit (CLP) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The CLP must be valid for no more than one year from the initial date of issuance without requiring the CLP holder to retake the general and endorsement knowledge tests.

questions.question: Under 383.25(a)(1), where must the accompanying CDL holder be when a CLP holder drives a CMV that is not a passenger vehicle?

options.A: In the sleeper berth, if the vehicle has one
options.B: In a vehicle following close enough to keep the CMV in sight
options.C: Within reach by radio or phone
options.D: Physically present in the front seat of the vehicle next to the CLP holder

questions.explanation: The CDL holder "must at all times be physically present in the front seat of the vehicle next to the CLP holder or, in the case of a passenger vehicle, directly behind or in the first row behind the driver" and must have the CLP holder "under observation and direct supervision."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.25, Commercial learner's permit (CLP) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The CDL holder must at all times be physically present in the front seat of the vehicle next to the CLP holder or, in the case of a passenger vehicle, directly behind or in the first row behind the driver and must have the CLP holder under observation and direct supervision.

questions.question: What may a CLP holder with a tank vehicle (N) endorsement operate?

options.A: A tank vehicle loaded with any cargo other than hazardous materials
options.B: A loaded tank vehicle, if the accompanying CDL holder has an N endorsement
options.C: Only an empty tank vehicle that, if it previously contained hazardous materials, has been purged of any residue
options.D: A tank vehicle filled to no more than half its capacity

questions.explanation: "A CLP holder with an N endorsement may only operate an empty tank vehicle and is prohibited from operating any tank vehicle that previously contained hazardous materials that has not been purged of any residue."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.25, Commercial learner's permit (CLP) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 383.91(a)(1), a combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more is a Group A combination vehicle provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed meets what condition set by the rule?

options.B: 10,000 pounds or less
options.C: In excess of 5,000 pounds
options.D: Any weight, if the towed vehicle has air brakes

questions.explanation: Group A is "Any combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating (GCWR) of 11,794 kilograms or more (26,001 pounds or more) provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is in excess of 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds)."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.91, Commercial motor vehicle groups (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (1) Combination vehicle (Group A)-Any combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating (GCWR) of 11,794 kilograms or more (26,001 pounds or more) provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is in excess of 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds).

questions.question: How does 383.91(a)(2) describe a Heavy Straight Vehicle (Group B)?

options.A: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 10,001 to 26,000 pounds
options.B: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or any such vehicle towing a vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR
options.C: Any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more towing more than 10,000 pounds
options.D: Any single vehicle designed to transport 9 to 15 passengers

questions.explanation: Group B is "Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 11,794 kilograms or more (26,001 pounds or more), or any such vehicle towing a vehicle not in excess of 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds) GVWR."

questions.question: Under 383.91(a)(3), a vehicle that meets neither the Group A nor the Group B definition is a Group C small vehicle if it is used to transport hazardous materials or if it meets what passenger threshold set by the rule?

options.A: Designed to transport 8 or more passengers, not counting the driver
options.B: Designed to transport 10 or more passengers, including the driver
options.C: Designed to transport 12 or more passengers, not counting the driver
options.D: Designed to transport 16 or more passengers including the driver

questions.explanation: Group C covers a vehicle that meets neither Group A nor Group B "but that either is designed to transport 16 or more passengers including the driver, or is used in the transportation of hazardous materials as defined in § 383.5."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.91, Commercial motor vehicle groups (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 383.153(a)(9), what does the endorsement code X stand for on a CDL?

options.B: Passenger
options.C: A combination of tank vehicle and hazardous materials endorsements
options.D: School bus

questions.explanation: The CDL endorsement codes include "X for a combination of tank vehicle and hazardous materials endorsements". Double/triple trailers is T, passenger is P and school bus is S.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.153, Information on the CLP and CDL documents and applications (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 383.95(c), what must the State indicate on the CDL, if issued, when the applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission?

options.A: That the person is restricted to intrastate operation
options.B: That the person is restricted from operating a CMV with a GVWR over 26,000 pounds
options.C: That the person must retake the skills test within one year
options.D: That the person is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with a manual transmission

questions.explanation: The State "must indicate on the CDL, if issued, that the person is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with a manual transmission." The CDL code for this restriction is "E for No Manual transmission equipped CMV".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.95, Restrictions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission, the State must indicate on the CDL, if issued, that the person is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with a manual transmission.

questions.question: Under 383.93(c), which endorsement requires both a knowledge test and a skills test?

options.B: Double/Triple Trailers
options.C: Tank vehicle
options.D: Hazardous Materials

questions.explanation: 383.93(c) lists "Passenger -a knowledge and a skills test" (school bus also requires both), while double/triple trailers, tank vehicle and hazardous materials each require "a knowledge test".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.93, Endorsements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (1) Double/Triple Trailers -a knowledge test; (2) Passenger -a knowledge and a skills test; (3) Tank vehicle -a knowledge test; (4) Hazardous Materials -a knowledge test; and (5) School bus -a knowledge and a skills test.

questions.question: Under Table 1 to 383.51, what disqualification applies to a first conviction for having an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater while operating a CMV transporting hazardous materials?

options.B: 120 days
options.C: 3 years
options.D: 10 years

questions.explanation: In Table 1, row (3) (alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater while operating a CMV) sets 1 year for a first conviction in a CMV and 3 years for a first conviction while operating a CMV transporting hazardous materials.

options.B: 120 days
options.C: 90 days
options.D: 10 years

questions.explanation: Table 2 sets 60 days for a second conviction and 120 days for a third or subsequent conviction of any combination of the listed offenses "in a separate incident within a 3-year period" while operating a CMV.

questions.question: What minimum disqualification period does Table 3 to 383.51 set for a first conviction when a driver who is always required to stop fails to stop before driving onto a railroad-highway grade crossing?

options.B: 30 days
options.C: 60 days
options.D: 1 year

questions.explanation: Table 3 row (3), "The driver is always required to stop, but fails to stop before driving onto the crossing", sets no less than 60 days for a first conviction, no less than 120 days for a second and no less than 1 year for a third or subsequent conviction within a 3-year period.

questions.question: What disqualification range does row (1) of Table 4 to 383.51 set for a first conviction of violating a driver or vehicle out-of-service order while transporting nonhazardous materials?

options.A: No less than 180 days or more than 1 year
options.B: No less than 10 days or more than 60 days
options.C: No less than 30 days or more than 90 days
options.D: No less than 1 year or more than 10 years

questions.question: What passing score does 383.135(a)(1) set for each CDL knowledge test?

options.A: Correctly answering at least 60 percent of the questions
options.B: Correctly answering at least 70 percent of the questions
options.C: Correctly answering at least 75 percent of the questions
options.D: Correctly answering at least 80 percent of the questions

questions.explanation: "To achieve a passing score on each of the knowledge tests, a driver applicant must correctly answer at least 80 percent of the questions."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.135, Passing knowledge and skills tests (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: To achieve a passing score on each of the knowledge tests, a driver applicant must correctly answer at least 80 percent of the questions.

questions.question: In what order does 383.133(c)(6) require the skills test to be administered and successfully completed?

options.A: On-road skills, basic vehicle control skills, pre-trip inspection
options.B: Pre-trip inspection, basic vehicle control skills, on-road skills
options.C: Basic vehicle control skills, pre-trip inspection, on-road skills
options.D: Pre-trip inspection, on-road skills, basic vehicle control skills

questions.explanation: "The skills test must be administered and successfully completed in the following order: Pre-trip inspection, basic vehicle control skills, on-road skills." An applicant who fails one segment "cannot continue to the next segment of the test".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 383.133, Test methods (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The skills test must be administered and successfully completed in the following order: Pre-trip inspection, basic vehicle control skills, on-road skills.
